memory_update.text: GEV, ETN, HUBB, PWR, and CLF should be tracked as the first-pass US-listed universe for grid transformers/interconnection: OEM grid equipment, electrical power equipment, T&D components, EPC labor/platform, and electrical steel input.

POWL is a strong near-miss candidate for the same node: custom-engineered electrical distribution/control equipment, substation automation via Remsdaq, $1.4B fiscal 2025 backlog, data-center and utility opportunity commentary. Consider adding if the dashboard allows more than five names.

Several major transformer/grid equipment leaders have non-primary or non-US listings or are subsidiaries, including Hitachi Energy/Hitachi, Siemens Energy, Schneider Electric, ABB, and private transformer manufacturers such as ERMCO and Howard Industries. This pass prioritized US-listed mappings.

The strongest falsification test for this node is whether transformer/switchgear lead times, book-to-bill, and EPC backlog normalize faster than expected; if backlog growth slows materially or pricing weakens, downgrade bottleneck quality.

Need a follow-up pass on software/data/control platforms for grid interconnection and automation, including ITRI, ROK, EMR, HON, and grid-planning software vendors; this pass emphasized direct hardware/EPC chokepoints.

node: Grid interconnection, transmission, substations, and transformers
summary: Focused expansion of US-listed names most directly exposed to the grid equipment and interconnection chokepoint. The highest-quality public-market mappings in this pass are: transformer/grid equipment OEMs, electrical power-management vendors, utility T&D component suppliers, grid EPC/labor platforms, and a less obvious but important materials supplier for transformer electrical steel. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
